app.name: Halal Scanner
home.intro: Scan the barcode of a food product. The app checks the ingredient list against transparent rules and explains the result.
home.recent.empty: No products checked yet. Your first scan will appear here.
home.disclaimer: This app does not replace halal certification or religious advice. Missing information is never treated as halal.

status.halalCertified.meaning: A valid, verified halal certificate was found for exactly this product.
status.halalByIngredients.meaning: All approval conditions are met: the complete ingredient list from the database was checked against the documented rules, and the origin of all critical ingredients is documented for this product. This is NOT a halal certification and no assurance about production, cross-contamination or undeclared components.
status.haram.meaning: A prohibited ingredient is explicitly listed in the product data.
status.unclear.meaning: The origin of at least one ingredient could not be documented despite research, or its assessment depends on a documented difference of scholarly opinion.
status.notVerified.meaning: The product, the complete ingredient list or decisive information is missing, incomplete, contradictory or not reliable enough. This is not an approval.

report.found.none: No problematic ingredients found in the checked information.
report.labelUnverified: A halal label is recorded in Open Food Facts. It was entered by database users and has not been verified; it is not treated as a certificate.
report.summary.haram: {items} was found in the available ingredient list. Therefore the product was classified as haram according to the defined criteria.
report.summary.unclear: The product contains {items}. Its origin was researched but could not be documented for this product, or the assessment is disputed. A reliable halal classification is not possible at the moment.
report.summary.halalByIngredients: All {count} ingredients were checked and all approval conditions are met. This is not a halal certification and no guarantee.
report.summary.halalCertified: A valid certification ({certifier}) was found for this product. Certifier, validity and product match are shown under “Sources and reasoning”.
report.issue.title: Report a problem
report.issue.body: Product data (name, ingredients) comes from Open Food Facts, where you can correct it directly – this helps everyone. You can report errors in the app's assessment to us. Your report does not change the result automatically.
report.issue.off: Correct product on Open Food Facts
finding.fromTag: Additive {code} according to database analysis (not detected in text)

evidence.ocr: Ingredient list photographed by the user and read automatically (not a verified record).
evidence.userEdited: Ingredient list entered or corrected by the user (not a verified record).
certainty.documented: Documented: the result is based on an explicit statement in the product data or on a verified certificate.
certainty.limited: Limited: the result is based only on the declared ingredient list. Production and origin of raw materials are not documented.
certainty.notAssessable: Not assessable: the available data is insufficient.
qualifier.halalStated: manufacturer's halal statement in the ingredient list
unknown.productNotFound: The product is not in Open Food Facts. You can photograph the ingredient list.
unknown.identityMismatch: The database returned a different product than the scanned barcode. The data was not used.
unknown.identityWeak: No product name is stored for this barcode, so the match is not unambiguous.
unknown.notIdentifiedPhotoOnly: The ingredients come from a photo. The product was not identified via a database.
unknown.ingredientsIncomplete: The data source marks the ingredient list as incomplete.
unknown.possiblyTruncated: The ingredient list may be cut off or not fully captured.
unknown.uncertainOcrText: Some text was recognized with low confidence.
unknown.userEditedText: The ingredient list was typed or corrected by hand and is not a verified record.
unknown.conflictingSources: The available information is contradictory (e.g. different ingredient lists in different languages, or certificate and ingredients do not match).
unknown.certificationExpired: A certificate was found but has expired or is not yet valid.
unknown.certificationNotApplicable: A certificate was found but does not apply to exactly this product.
unknown.certificationUnverified: A certificate reference could not be verified.
unknown.dataOld: The product data has not been updated for more than 3 years. The recipe may have changed.
unknown.manufacturingNotVerified: Production methods, origin of raw materials and possible contamination were not checked.
unknown.languageNotSupported: The ingredient list is only available in a language for which this app has no rules yet (supported: German, English, French, Turkish).
rule.pork.name: Pork
rule.pork.why: Pork and all pig-derived ingredients are prohibited under all recognized halal standards.
rule.porkDerived.name: {item} from pork
rule.porkDerived.why: The ingredient is stated to come from pork and is therefore not halal.
rule.blood.name: Blood
rule.blood.why: Blood as a food ingredient is prohibited under recognized halal standards.
rule.alcoholic_beverage.name: Alcoholic beverage
rule.alcoholic_beverage.why: Wine, beer, spirits and similar drinks are not permitted as ingredients under the criteria used. Whether residues after cooking are assessed differently is debated; the app cautiously classifies an explicitly listed ingredient as haram.
rule.alcohol_declared.name: Alcohol (ethanol)
rule.alcohol_declared.why: Alcohol is explicitly listed as an ingredient. Under the criteria used, added alcohol is not halal. Some standards allow technical trace amounts – this cannot be checked here.
rule.alcohol_free_beverage.name: Alcohol-free beer/wine
rule.alcohol_free_beverage.why: Alcohol-free beers and wines may contain residual alcohol and are made from alcoholic drinks. Assessments differ.
rule.wine_vinegar.name: Wine or balsamic vinegar
rule.wine_vinegar.why: Many scholars consider vinegar made from wine permissible after complete transformation, others do not. It is therefore shown as unclear.
rule.gelatine.name: Gelatine/collagen
rule.gelatine.why: Gelatine and collagen are made from animal skin or bones (mostly pork or beef) or from fish. Without the animal species and slaughter method no classification is possible.
rule.rennet.name: Rennet/enzymes
rule.rennet.why: Rennet and enzymes can be of animal (e.g. calf stomach), microbial or plant origin. The origin is not stated.
rule.cheese.name: Cheese
rule.cheese.why: Cheese is often made with rennet of animal origin. The type of rennet is not stated.
rule.meat.name: Meat (slaughter or species unclear)
rule.meat.why: Meat of permitted animals is only halal if slaughtered according to Islamic rules. This cannot be proven from the ingredient list. For sausage, ham, bacon or salami the animal species is also often not stated.
rule.animal_fat.name: Animal fat
rule.animal_fat.why: Animal fats (e.g. tallow, lard) may come from pigs or from animals not slaughtered ritually. The origin is not stated.
rule.flavouring.name: Flavouring
rule.flavouring.why: Flavourings may contain animal components or alcohol as a solvent or carrier. Manufacturers do not have to declare this fully.
rule.e_number_animal_possible.name: Additive of possible animal origin
rule.e_number_animal_possible.why: Substances like E471 (mono- and diglycerides), glycerol, stearates, polysorbates or L-cysteine (E920) can be made from plants, synthetically or from animals. Without the origin no classification is possible.
rule.bone_phosphate.name: Bone phosphate (E542)
rule.bone_phosphate.why: Made from animal bones. Species and slaughter are not stated.
rule.insect_derived.name: Insect-derived ingredient
rule.insect_derived.why: Insect-derived substances (e.g. carmine E120, shellac E904) are assessed differently by scholars and halal standards.
rule.seafood_non_fish.name: Seafood (not fish)
rule.seafood_non_fish.why: Shrimp, mussels, squid and similar are assessed differently depending on the school of law, particularly in the Hanafi school.
rule.whey.name: Whey
rule.whey.why: Whey is a by-product of cheese making. Some halal standards check the origin of the rennet. This note does not change the result.

ingredients.none.title: No ingredient list
ingredients.none.body: No ingredient list is available for this product. You can photograph or type it.
ingredients.edit.note: Your correction is checked separately. The original data remains unchanged. Text typed by hand can never result in a halal approval.

sources.decision.haram: Rule A: a prohibited ingredient is explicitly named in the data.
sources.decision.halalCertified: Rule B: a verified certificate matches barcode, manufacturer and validity period.

sources.rulesBody: Rule version {version}, applied on {date}. The rules are fixed in code and covered by test cases. No AI makes the decision.
sources.limitsBody: Only what is written in the ingredient list is checked. Not checked: slaughter, origin of raw materials, production facilities, contamination and undeclared processing aids. Halal labels from the database do not count as certificates.
ocr.title: Photograph ingredients
ocr.frame: Photograph only the ingredient list – complete, straight and sharp.
ocr.tips.title: Tips for a good photo
ocr.tips.body:
• Good light, no reflections
• Hold the phone parallel to the package
• The whole list must be visible, including the heading “Ingredients”
• Currently only Latin script is recognized
ocr.privacy: Text recognition runs entirely on your phone. The photo is deleted immediately afterwards and never uploaded.

ocr.review.title: Recognized text
ocr.review.body: Please compare the text with the package. You can correct errors – the result will then be marked as “entered by hand”.
ocr.confirmComplete: The complete ingredient list is visible in the photo and the text is correct.
ocr.notice: A photo of the ingredient list does not prove the origin of raw materials or production conditions. Without a database record a photo never results in a halal approval.

info.rules.title: How the app checks
info.rules.body:
1. The barcode identifies the product. Data is loaded from Open Food Facts – only for exactly this barcode. Open Food Facts is a free database, not a certification body.

2. The ingredient list is split into individual ingredients (including sub-ingredients) and compared with a fixed, versioned rule list. No AI makes the decision.

3. For every critical ingredient the app researches automatically: substance identity and E number, the product's structured ingredient data, origin statements in the list (e.g. “plant-based”), package labels (vegan/vegetarian), general substance data from the Open Food Facts taxonomy and available manufacturer links. A question only counts as clarified if there is information about exactly this product. General substance information and user notes never clarify anything.

4. Result:
• RED – HARAM: a prohibited ingredient is explicitly named (e.g. pork, pork gelatine, blood, wine, alcohol).
• ORANGE – UNCLEAR: the origin of an ingredient could not be documented despite research (e.g. gelatine without details, flavouring, E471, rennet, meat without halal statement) or the assessment is disputed among scholars (e.g. carmine, wine vinegar, seafood).
• GREY – NOT VERIFIED: the product, the complete ingredient list or decisive information is missing, incomplete, contradictory, only photographed or typed by hand.
• GREEN – HALAL BY COMPLETE INGREDIENT CHECK: only if all approval conditions are met (checklist in the result). This is not a certification and no guarantee.
• HALAL CERTIFIED only appears with a verified, valid certificate for exactly this product. No free, verifiable certificate source is connected at the moment.

Missing information is never treated as halal.

Important: the rules are a technical implementation of cautious, widely held principles. They have not yet been reviewed by Islamic scholars. If in doubt, ask a person with religious expertise.
info.privacy.title: Privacy
info.privacy.body:
• No registration, no account, no ads, no analytics.
• When scanning, only the barcode number is sent to Open Food Facts (world.openfoodfacts.org); for ingredient research also general substance identifiers (e.g. “en:e471”) – no personal data to retrieve product data. Like any internet connection, the server sees your IP address.
• Product images are loaded directly from Open Food Facts.
• Photos of ingredient lists are processed only on your phone and deleted immediately afterwards.
• History, favorites and settings are stored only locally on your phone. You can delete them in the settings at any time or by uninstalling the app.
• Camera: used only for scanning and taking photos.

Open Food Facts privacy policy: https://world.openfoodfacts.org/privacy
info.sources.title: Data sources and licenses
info.sources.body:
Product data: Open Food Facts – a free, collaboratively maintained database. The database is licensed under the Open Database License (ODbL), individual contents under the Database Contents License, product images under Creative Commons BY-SA. The data is entered by volunteers and may be incomplete or outdated. You can correct errors directly on openfoodfacts.org.

Barcode recognition: mobile_scanner (BSD-3-Clause) with Google ML Kit (Android) or Apple Vision (iPhone).
Text recognition: Google ML Kit Text Recognition – runs offline on the device.

Halal certificates: no free, verifiable certificate database is currently connected. Halal labels from Open Food Facts are shown but not treated as certificates.

Source code: github.com/koray26/halal-scanner
green.intro.met: A green result is only given when all of these conditions are met:
green.intro.unmet: These approval conditions are not met:
green.notGuarantee: Note: this is not a halal certification and no guarantee. Production, cross-contamination and undeclared components were not checked.
green.cond.databaseSource: Ingredients come from the product database (not only photo or manual entry)
green.cond.languageSupported: Language and script of the ingredient list are supported
green.cond.listComplete: Ingredient list complete and not cut off
green.cond.dataPlausible: Data plausible (no data quality warnings from the database)
green.cond.allOriginsClarified: Origin of all critical ingredients documented for this product
green.cond.noDisputedSubstance: No substance with a documented difference of opinion
inv.intro: Tap an ingredient to see the full research.
inv.possibleOrigins: Possible origins (general – NOT documented for this product): {list}
inv.q.productEvidence: What is documented for this product?
inv.noProductEvidence: No origin information was found for this product.
inv.generalNote: This information applies to the substance in general and does not prove what it is made of in this product.
inv.disputedNote: The assessment depends on a difference of opinion. Product data cannot settle this, so the app gives no approval.
inv.q.clarify: Which information would clarify the classification?
question.animalSource: Does the substance come from (slaughtered) animals?
question.animalSpecies: Is pork excluded as the animal species?
question.slaughter: Was it slaughtered according to Islamic rules?
question.alcohol: Is alcohol (e.g. as solvent or carrier) excluded?
clarify.animalSource: Manufacturer statement on origin, e.g. “plant-based”, “microbial” or a vegan label
clarify.animalSpecies: Statement of the animal species (e.g. “beef”, “fish”) or “pork-free”
clarify.slaughter: Proof of halal origin or a valid halal certificate for the raw material
clarify.alcohol: Manufacturer statement “without alcohol” or the solvent/carrier used
clarify.scholarlyDispute: A ruling according to the school of law or standard you follow – product data cannot settle this
inquiry.q.animalSource: Is this component of animal origin? If so, from which animal?
inquiry.q.animalSpecies: Which animal species does the component come from? Is pork excluded?
inquiry.q.slaughter: Is there halal proof for the animal raw material?
inquiry.q.alcohol: Is alcohol (ethanol) used as a solvent or carrier?
inquiry.buttonAll: Prepare an inquiry to the manufacturer
inquiry.subject: Question about ingredients: {product}
evidence.structured: Database ingredient analysis: identified as “{id}” (general classification vegan: {vegan}, vegetarian: {vegetarian}).
evidence.qualifier.plant: The ingredient list states a plant origin: “{ingredient}”
evidence.qualifier.synthetic: The ingredient list states synthetic production: “{ingredient}”
evidence.qualifier.nonAnimalEnzyme: The ingredient list states a microbial/non-animal origin: “{ingredient}”
evidence.qualifier.fish: The ingredient list states fish as the origin: “{ingredient}”
evidence.qualifier.halalStated: Manufacturer statement “halal” in the ingredient list: “{ingredient}” (manufacturer claim, not a verified certificate)
evidence.labelVegan: Package label “vegan” according to the database (entered by users) – excludes animal origin, but not alcohol.
evidence.labelVegetarian: Package label “vegetarian” according to the database (entered by users) – excludes components from slaughtered animals.
evidence.labelContradiction: Contradiction: the package is labelled “{label}” according to the database, which does not fit this ingredient.
evidence.taxonomy: Open Food Facts taxonomy “{name}” ({id}): in general vegan: {vegan}, vegetarian: {vegetarian}.
evidence.manufacturerLink: Manufacturer page listed in the database. It is not evaluated automatically (no open interface) – please check it yourself.
step.productIngredients: Structured ingredient data of the product
step.ingredientText: Origin statements in the ingredient list
step.taxonomy: General substance data (Open Food Facts taxonomy, online)
resolution.qualifier.plant: plant origin stated in the ingredient list
resolution.qualifier.halalStated: manufacturer's halal statement in the ingredient list
unknown.languageMismatch: According to the database the language of the ingredient list does not match the declared language. The data may be faulty.
unknown.ingredientsMostlyUnrecognized: The database could not identify most ingredients. The list may have been captured incorrectly.
unknown.labelContradiction: A package label (e.g. “vegan”) contradicts an ingredient. The information is contradictory.
unknown.researchSourceUnavailable: A research source was unreachable (e.g. offline). This check was not performed – please “Check again” later.
unknown.unsupportedScript: The photo probably contains a script that text recognition cannot read.
ocr.unsupportedScript: The recognized text does not look like Latin script. Text recognition currently only supports Latin script – please check and correct the text or type it. A green approval is not possible this way.
substance.pork.identity: Component from pigs (meat, fat, skin or substances derived from them).
substance.blood.identity: Blood or blood components of animals.
substance.alcoholic_beverage.identity: Beverage produced by fermentation (possibly distillation) that contains ethanol, e.g. wine, beer, spirits.
substance.alcohol_declared.identity: Ethanol (drinking alcohol) – chemically well defined. The raw material source is usually not stated.
substance.alcohol_free_beverage.identity: Beer or wine from which most of the alcohol was removed. “Alcohol-free” can mean small residual amounts depending on the country (customary in Germany up to 0.5 % vol).
substance.wine_vinegar.identity: Vinegar made from wine by acetic fermentation; the alcohol is largely converted into acetic acid.
substance.gelatine.identity: Protein from collagen, obtained from skin, bones or connective tissue of animals (mostly pork or beef) or from fish. The species is not always stated in the ingredient list.
substance.rennet.identity: Enzyme mixture (mainly chymosin) used to curdle milk. It can come from calf stomachs, microorganisms or plants.
substance.cheese.identity: Made from milk; rennet of animal or microbial origin is often used for curdling.
substance.meat.identity: Meat or meat product. The species is not always stated, the slaughter method usually never.
substance.animal_fat.identity: Fat from animal tissue, e.g. tallow (beef) or lard (pork, goose).
substance.flavouring.identity: Collective term for substances that add smell or taste. Under EU law the individual flavouring substances and carriers (e.g. ethanol) generally do not have to be listed.
substance.e_number_animal_possible.ident: Additive with a known chemical identity that can be made from plant or animal raw materials or synthetically. The raw material source does not have to be stated.
substance.bone_phosphate.identity: Calcium phosphate obtained from animal bones.
substance.insect_derived.identity: Substance from insects, e.g. carmine from scale insects or shellac from the secretion of lac insects.
substance.seafood_non_fish.identity: Crustaceans or molluscs, e.g. shrimp, mussels or squid.
substance.whey.identity: Liquid produced when making cheese or quark.
